tickets.title: Local Resolution Override
tickets.summary: A developer cannot reach 'webapp.local' (10.0.0.50). Pinging the name returns 127.0.0.1, even though DNS is correct on the server.

triage.q: If Nslookup is correct but Ping is wrong, what does this indicate about the resolution process?
options: The client is using a local override (Hosts file)

diagnosis.q: Which file on a Windows system takes priority over DNS server queries for name resolution?

fix.q: How do you restore correct network resolution for this client?
options: Remove the 'webapp.local' entry from the local Hosts file

debrief.summary: The 'Hosts' file is checked before DNS. If an entry exists there, the client will never ask the DNS server.
debrief.takeaway: Always compare Nslookup (direct DNS query) vs Ping (standard OS resolution) to find local overrides.

tickets.title: SRV Record Registration Failure
tickets.summary: A secondary Domain Controller (DC-02) was added, but clients cannot authenticate against it. It is missing from the _msdcs zone.
artifact: Evidence: DC-02 is missing from the _ldap._tcp records
DC-02 Status: Server is online and reachable by IP

triage.q: Which DNS record type is used by Active Directory to locate Domain Controllers?

diagnosis.q: What service is responsible for registering these SRV records on a Domain Controller?

fix.q: How can you force a Domain Controller to re-register its missing SRV records in DNS?
options: Delete the DNS zone and recreate it

debrief.summary: Active Directory relies on Service (SRV) records to point clients to available Domain Controllers.
debrief.takeaway: Restarting the Netlogon service triggers a dynamic update that re-registers all required AD service records.
